content.text:
### RetryOptions Interface

Source: https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.RetryOptions.html

The RetryOptions interface allows you to configure how job retries are handled. You can specify whether to reset attempt counters when retrying.

```APIDOC
## Interface RetryOptions

Retry method options

```typescript
interface RetryOptions {
  resetAttemptsMade?: boolean;
  resetAttemptsStarted?: boolean;
}
```

### Properties

*   **`resetAttemptsMade`** (`boolean`, optional): Attempts made counter is reset to zero when retrying the job.
*   **`resetAttemptsStarted`** (`boolean`, optional): Attempts started counter is reset to zero when retrying the job.
```

--------------------------------

### v5 > RetryOptions

Source: https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.RetryOptions.html

The RetryOptions interface in BullMQ allows configuration of how retry counters are managed when a job is retried. By default, these counters are not reset. Setting `resetAttemptsMade` to true will reset the attempts made counter to zero upon retry. Similarly, setting `resetAttemptsStarted` to true will reset the attempts started counter to zero upon retry.

--------------------------------

### Job Class > getState

Source: https://api.docs.bullmq.io/classes/v5.Job.html

The `getState` method retrieves the current state of a job. Possible states include 'completed', 'failed', 'delayed', 'active', 'waiting', 'waiting-children', and 'unknown'.

--------------------------------

### MinimalJob Interface

Source: https://api.docs.bullmq.io/interfaces/v5.MinimalJob.html

This interface defines the structure and available operations for a minimal job object in BullMQ.

### reprocessJob

Source: https://api.docs.bullmq.io/classes/v5.Scripts.html

Attempts to reprocess a job that has failed or completed. The job is moved back to the waiting queue for another attempt.

```APIDOC
## reprocessJob

### Description
Attempts to reprocess a job that has failed or completed.

### Method
reprocessJob

### Type Parameters
* **T** - Type of the job data.
* **R** - Type of the job return value.
* **N** - Type of the job name.

### Parameters
* **job** (MinimalJob<T, R, N>) - The job to reprocess.
* **state** (string) - The expected job state. Supported states: 'failed', 'completed'.
* **opts** (RetryOptions) - Optional retry options.

### Returns
Promise<void> - A promise that resolves when the job has been successfully moved to the wait queue.

### Throws
Will throw an error with a code property indicating the failure reason:
* **code 0**: Job does not exist
* **code -1**: Job is currently locked and can't be retried
* **code -2**: Job was not found in the expected set
```

content.text:
### Pessimistic write locking with setLock

Source: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/docs/docs/query-builder/1-select-query-builder.md

Use setLock("pessimistic_write") to acquire an exclusive lock on the selected rows. Supported on all listed databases.

```typescript
const users = await dataSource
    .getRepository(User)
    .createQueryBuilder("user")
    .setLock("pessimistic_write")
    .getMany()
```

--------------------------------

### getRawOne: Fetch a single raw result

Source: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/docs/docs/query-builder/1-select-query-builder.md

Use getRawOne to retrieve a single raw data result, such as a sum of user photos. This is for non-entity data.

```typescript
const { sum } = await dataSource
    .getRepository(User)
    .createQueryBuilder("user")
    .select("SUM(user.photosCount)", "sum")
    .where("user.id = :id", { id: 1 })
    .getRawOne()
```

--------------------------------

### Getting values using `QueryBuilder`

Source: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/docs/docs/query-builder/1-select-query-builder.md

There are two types of results you can get using select query builder: **entities** or **raw results**.
Most of the time, you need to select real entities from your database, for example, users.
For this purpose, you use `getOne` and `getMany`.
But sometimes you need to select some specific data, let's say the _sum of all user photos_.
This data is not an entity, it's called raw data.
To get raw data, you use `getRawOne` and `getRawMany`.

--------------------------------

### Create transaction using EntityManager

Source: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/docs/docs/transactions.mdx

Starts a transaction using the EntityManager's `transaction` method. The callback receives a `transactionalEntityManager` that must be used for all operations within the transaction.

```typescript
await myDataSource.manager.transaction(async (transactionalEntityManager) => {
    // execute queries using transactionalEntityManager
})
```

--------------------------------

### Transactions > Creating and using transactions

Source: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/docs/docs/transactions.mdx

Transactions are created using `DataSource` or `EntityManager`.
Examples:

```typescript
await myDataSource.transaction(async (transactionalEntityManager) => {
    // execute queries using transactionalEntityManager
})
```

or

```typescript
await myDataSource.manager.transaction(async (transactionalEntityManager) => {
    // execute queries using transactionalEntityManager
})
```

Everything you want to run in a transaction must be executed in a callback:

```typescript
await myDataSource.manager.transaction(async (transactionalEntityManager) => {
    await transactionalEntityManager.save(users)
    await transactionalEntityManager.save(photos)
    // ...
})
```

The most important restriction when working in a transaction is to **ALWAYS** use the provided instance of entity manager -
`transactionalEntityManager` in this example. DO NOT USE GLOBAL ENTITY MANAGER.
All operations **MUST** be executed using the provided transactional entity manager.
